name: Soy milk (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Soy milk [Soy] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, PHENOL EXPLORER, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FoodData Central - Soymilk, original and vanilla, unfortified (SR Legacy NDB 16223)
Nielsen et al. 2024, Regional Variability in Sugar/AA Content of U.S. Soybeans, PMC11202694
Valliyodan et al. 2015, Chromatography Research Int'l, doi:10.1155/2015/757649 (soybean sugars)
Zhang et al. 2020, Food Production Processing and Nutrition, doi:10.1186/s43014-020-00021-1 (soybean organic acids)
PubMed 25466130 - soluble sugars, organic acids, minerals in milk/soy-juice beverages
ScienceDirect S1756464623001950 - low-phytate soymilk phytic acid 2.61 g/kg
Omogbai et al. - stachyose in soymilk yogurt (initial ~330 mg/100 mL)
Massey - Oxalate and Phytate of Soy Foods (Iowa State)
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy sources for a microbe growing on plain soymilk are sucrose (chief fermentable free sugar) plus the raffinose-family oligosaccharides stachyose and raffinose (fermentable only by alpha-galactosidase-positive organisms), with soy protein and its amino acids (Glu/Asp-rich) as the dominant organic-nitrogen source; organic acids (malic, citric, phytic) are minor. Profile is for UNFORTIFIED plain soymilk - calcium (25 vs ~120 mg), vitamin B12, vitamin D and vitamin A are essenti

curation_removed.name: Caffeine
curation_removed.reason: not a soybean constituent; FooDB cross-contamination/misassignment. Soymilk contains no caffeine (only chocolate/tea-flavored variants would)

curation_removed.name: Theobromine
curation_removed.reason: not a soybean constituent; methylxanthine from cacao/tea, FooDB noise, biologically implausible in plain soymilk

curation_removed.name: (R)-Oxypeucedanin
curation_removed.reason: furanocoumarin of Apiaceae/citrus, not soy; FooDB predicted/misassigned, implausible in soy matrix

curation_removed.name: Retinol
curation_removed.reason: animal-form vitamin A; native unfortified soymilk retinol activity ~0. Present only in vitamin-A-fortified products

curation_removed.name: Cyanocobalamin (B12)
curation_removed.reason: native soymilk B12 = 0 (plants do not synthesize B12); appears only via fortification. Not a native growth nutrient of the food

curation_removed.name: Vitamin D / Ergocalciferol
curation_removed.reason: native soymilk vitamin D = 0; present only in D-fortified products. Ergocalciferol in the uncovered list is a fortification/predicted artifact, not native

curation_removed.name: D-Serine
curation_removed.reason: stereochemistry artifact; soy protein serine is L-Serine. Replaced by L-Serine in components

composition_provenance.definition: sourced = the cited source states this component; derived = the pipeline supplied it. Classification table: tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv.

components.name: sucrose
components.evidence_source: USDA FDC soymilk unsweetened total sugars 0.56 g (predominantly sucrose); Valliyodan 2015 doi:10.1155/2015/757649 (sucrose is the dominant free soybean sugar)

components.name: stachyose
components.evidence_source: Soymilk oligosaccharide study (initial stachyose ~330 mg/100 mL before fermentation; Omogbai et al.); soybean 1.34 g/100g (Nielsen 2024 PMC11202694)

components.name: raffinose
components.evidence_source: Soymilk RFO range 30-274 mg/100 mL; soybean 0.34 g/100g (PMC11202694)

components.name: D-glucose
components.evidence_source: soybean free glucose 0.07-0.43 g/100g (PMC11202694), heavily diluted in soymilk

components.name: D-fructose
components.evidence_source: soybean free fructose 0.08-0.21 g/100g (PMC11202694), heavily diluted

components.name: citric acid
components.evidence_source: soybean organic-acid profile: citric among predominant acids (Zhang 2020 doi:10.1186/s43014-020-00021-1); soy-beverage HPLC (PubMed 25466130)

components.name: malic acid
components.evidence_source: malic is the main organic acid of (vegetable) soybean, > citric (Zhang 2020 doi:10.1186/s43014-020-00021-1)

components.name: oxalic acid
components.evidence_source: Oxalate & Phytate of Soy Foods (Iowa State, Massey)

components.name: oleic acid
components.evidence_source: USDA FDC soymilk unfortified (total MUFA 0.40 g, ~all oleic)

components.name: L-Cysteine
components.evidence_source: soy protein Cys ~1.3% of protein (FAO soy AA scoring); USDA lists cystine 0 for this diluted item

components.name: Iodine
components.evidence_source: current record; native soy iodine very low

components.name: Nickel
components.evidence_source: current record; legumes accumulate Ni (urease cofactor)

components.name: Folate
components.evidence_source: USDA FDC soymilk unfortified (DFE; unsweetened 20 ug)

oxygen_note: food substrate; O2 availability is a simulation condition, not a property of the food
basis: per 100 g fresh weight (unfortified plain soymilk; ~ per 100 mL, density ~1.02); mM computed as (mg/100g x 10)/MW assuming density 1.0

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
